defects.what: The docstring says a title that "lost a heading renamed to a longer one" is caught. The meaning is right but the wording is garbled: it is the heading that was renamed, not the title that lost something. Rewording it like the reference ("a title cut short or a heading renamed to a longer one is caught") fixes the one line.

structured_output.summary:
`title_ok` now does what the reference does. A title that is a whole heading must be a heading of the doc it names, and a title that only starts some heading is a miss. The reference's single `return t in heads` under the prefix branch gives the same result. The author's version splits it into two branches, with a comment saying why the text fallback is skipped. Whether that counts as changing the `t in text` fallback is debatable, but the report names it and explains it as the brief asks.

The five quoted titles now match the full headings, which I confirmed exist: current-match.md:33 and :627, frontend.md:599 and :903. The script passes on the tree with 0 misses, so no cut-short citation is left. Only the quoted titles were edited. The lines were not reflowed, which the brief's "nothing else on the line" requires; the reference reflowed them.

No test was added. The brief's allowed files leave out tests/ and its done-when is the script run itself. Ruff passes and pytest passes.

The report's file:line, old-title and new-title table matches the diff. It also says that pytest was skipped (the objective run passed anyway) and what was not verified. The only defect is one awkward phrase in the new docstring.
